title: fleet upgrade counts an estate whose upgrade held back edited files as upgraded, and prints nothing about them
body:
Found by dc on 2026-09-16, reading the result of the 0069 fleet sweep (`bin/devbin fleet upgrade --apply` from `26ec799`). Reproduced.

The sweep reported:

    16 upgraded (16 needed a second pass to converge provenance), 0 FAILED

Laksa was one of the 16. Its own upgrade, re-run by hand from the same prefix, says:

    skipped    bin/devbin (edited in place -- upgrade with --force to replace it)
    skipped    bin/.devbin/lib/runlog (edited in place -- upgrade with --force to replace it)
    0 added, 0 updated, 40 unchanged, 0 removed, 2 skipped

Both are committed local patches in Laksa (`2e4fb6642`, `25c431a00`, 2026-09-12). Holding them is `upgrade` working as designed, and `devbin doctor` in Laksa reports them (`FAIL manifest: vendored files have been edited in place`). **What `fleet upgrade` does with that report is discard it**: `upgrade_one` runs each estate's upgrade with `>/dev/null 2>&1`, then decides `upgraded` from the exit code and the recorded provenance alone. The upgrade exits 0 with files skipped, and the manifest's `source_commit` is rewritten to the new commit regardless, so a partially upgraded estate is counted exactly like a whole one.

The consequence in this sweep is concrete: Laksa's `lib/runlog` does not carry `0065`'s `log:` decline (`gate_log_suffix`), although its manifest names `26ec799` as its source commit.

## Why it is worth an issue

A fleet summary is read INSTEAD of sixteen upgrade logs; that is its purpose. A count that folds "some files held back" into "upgraded" is a population filter with no marker -- the reader has no way to learn from the summary that one estate is not level.

## Shape of a fix, not a ruling

Keep each estate's upgrade output (or at least its `N skipped` count), report an estate with skipped files as its own outcome -- `upgraded, N held` with the paths -- and count it separately in the summary line. Hold it with an arm: a fixture estate with one vendored file edited in place, swept, asserting the summary does not count it as a clean upgrade and names the held file.
